name: STM6601DS2BDM6F
title: STM6600, STM6601: push-button power on/off controllers with power-on lockout, Smart Reset and 1.5 V reference
summary: A push-button power controller for battery equipment, 1.6 V to 5.5 V. A debounced press of /PB with the battery above the lockout threshold VTH+ asserts an enable output that switches the system's regulator, MOSFET or DC-DC converter on; the processor must then hold PSHOLD high to keep it on. In normal operation a press raises an interrupt, an undervoltage raises it too, and a long press of /PB with /SR either resets the processor or removes power, by option. It also carries a 1.5 V, 1 % reference, an undervoltage output /VCCLO and a button-state output /PBOUT, and draws 6 µA running and 0.6 µA in standby, in a 2 x 3 mm TDFN12. STM6601DS2BDM6F is the STM6601 (power-up timed by tON_BLANK) with an active-low /EN output, long push deasserting /EN, a pull-up on /SR, VTH+ 3.40 V, VTH- 3.20 V and tON_BLANK 1.4 s min.
key_figures: 6.0 µA typ, 8.0 µA max at 3.6 V; standby 0.6 µA typ, 1.0 µA max
2.50, 3.10, 3.30, 3.40 or 3.50 V typ by option (3.40 V for STM6601DS2BDM6F)
TDFN12, 2 x 3 mm, 0.75 mm typ high

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply, also the voltage watched against VTH+ and VTH-. Decouple to ground with 0.1 µF placed next to the pin.

pins.name: /SR
pins.function: Smart Reset button input, active low, ±8 kV HBM. Pressed together with /PB for the long-push time it resets or powers down, by option. A 100 kΩ pull-up is fitted on some options. Can be driven by a switch to ground or by an open-drain output (preferred, can share the line) or a push-pull output. Watched for a falling edge after power-up; it must not be held at ground permanently.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: 1.5 V reference output, ±1 %. Valid once /RST has been released (after tREC); off in standby. A capacitor to ground is required whether VREF is used or not; 1 µF is the recommended value.

pins.name: PSHOLD
pins.function: Power-supply hold input from the processor, compared against an internal reference. Driven high during start-up it confirms the power-up and keeps the enable output on; driven low in normal operation it turns the enable output off. A 300 kΩ pull-down is connected inside during start-up only.

pins.name: CSRD
pins.function: Smart Reset delay capacitor to ground, charged by ISRD; tSRD ends when it reaches VSRD. A low-ESR (ceramic) part is the recommended type. With no capacitor fitted, tSRD is zero and the long-push action follows directly once tINT_Min ends.

pins.name: /PB
pins.function: Power-on push-button input, active low, ±8 kV HBM, 100 kΩ internal pull-up. Needs a switch to ground (button or open-drain output) so the input swings from VCC to below VIL. A press held for tDEBOUNCE with VCC above VTH+ turns the enable output on; in normal operation a short press raises /INT, and a long press with /SR resets or powers down by option.

pins.name: /VCCLO
pins.function: Undervoltage output, active low, open drain: low while VCC is under VTH+ during power-up and whenever undervoltage is seen in normal operation. Floats in standby. Needs a pull-up; 10 kΩ suits most uses.

pins.name: /PBOUT
pins.function: Debounced state of /PB, active low, open drain. Goes low for a press lasting tDEBOUNCE, stays low at least tINT_Min, and returns high on release after that. Presses during undervoltage are ignored. On the STM6601 only the first press during start-up is passed until tON_BLANK ends. Needs a pull-up; 10 kΩ suits most uses.

pins.name: EN or /EN
pins.function: Enable output for the system supply, push-pull; EN active high or /EN active low by option (/EN on STM6601DS2BDM6F). Turns on after a valid, confirmed press; turns off on a failed start-up confirmation, PSHOLD low, undervoltage longer than tSRD + tINT_Min + tDEBOUNCE, a long push (enable-off options), or PSHOLD not high when tON_BLANK ends after a long-push reset (reset options).

pins.name: /RST
pins.function: Reset output, active low, open drain. Low for tREC at start-up after a valid press, and after a long push on the reset options. Needs a pull-up; 10 kΩ suits most uses.

pins.name: /INT
pins.function: Interrupt output, active low, open drain. In normal operation it goes low when VCC falls under VTH-, or after a /PB press of tDEBOUNCE, staying low while the button is held and for at least tINT_Min. Held high during power-up. Needs a pull-up; 10 kΩ suits most uses.

circuits.title: Application hookup
circuits.description: A battery feeds VCC (0.1 µF to ground), the system's DC-DC converter, power MOSFET or regulator, and an LED through R1 whose cathode returns to /VCCLO. The enable output switches the converter, whose output VDD powers the processor and the pull-ups R3, R4 and R5 on /RST, /INT and /PBOUT. /RST goes to the processor reset, /INT to its NMI or interrupt input, /PBOUT to an I/O pin, and an I/O pin drives PSHOLD back. Two buttons to ground serve /PB and /SR; CSRD to ground sets the Smart Reset delay; CREF on VREF is required, and VREF is available to the system.

operation.text: The controller turns the system supply on and off from three things: the state of the buttons, the PSHOLD line from the processor, and the battery voltage on VCC.

A press of /PB starts power-up only if it lasts tDEBOUNCE and VCC stays above VTH+ for that whole time; if VCC dips under VTH+ the count restarts once VCC is back above it. Then the enable output turns on, /RST goes low for tREC, and the processor boots and raises PSHOLD. Because processor pins are often high-impedance before they are set up, PSHOLD has an internal 300 kΩ pull-down during start-up. While power-up is in progress the button, /INT and undervoltage detection are not acted on, and /INT stays high.

On the STM6600 the button must stay pressed until PSHOLD goes high. PSHOLD is sampled at button release, or when tON_BLANK runs out if the button is still held then; if it is low the enable output is turned off at once. The button-press time is therefore the time allowed for the system to start, and tON_BLANK limits it so a stuck button or a hung processor cannot drain the battery.

On the STM6601 the button can be let go early; PSHOLD is ignored during tON_BLANK and sampled when it ends. Low at that moment, the enable output turns off at once, and releasing the button afterwards does not prevent it. The button, /INT and undervoltage are not acted on during the whole tON_BLANK. This guards against switching the system on with a faulty power switch or a processor that does not respond.

In normal operation (PSHOLD high), a /PB press longer than tDEBOUNCE drives /INT low for at least tINT_Min. Wired to the processor's interrupt or NMI input, this lets software save its state and switch off by pulling PSHOLD low.
The processor can pull PSHOLD low at any time in normal operation; the enable output then turns off, within the PSHOLD to enable propagation delay.

When VCC falls under VTH- in normal operation, /INT and /VCCLO go low. If VCC is back above VTH+ before tDEBOUNCE + tINT_Min + tSRD have passed, power stays on; if the undervoltage lasts that long, the enable output turns off and /PB is again watched for a normal start. /PBOUT shows whether an interrupt came from the button or from undervoltage, since it ignores the button during undervoltage.

operation.topic: Long push: hardware reset or power-down
operation.text: If the system hangs, holding /PB and /SR together for longer than tDEBOUNCE + tINT_Min + tSRD either pulses /RST low for tREC (reset options) or turns the enable output off (enable-off options). tSRD counts once both buttons have been held through their debounce, whichever was pressed first; any release stops the count. On reset options PSHOLD must be high again when tON_BLANK runs out after the reset, otherwise the enable output turns off. On enable-off options, /PB is watched again for a new start after tEN_OFF.
With the enable output off the part is in standby, drawing 0.6 µA typ. Only a falling edge on /PB is watched, the 1.5 V reference is switched off and /VCCLO floats.

Pulses on /PB shorter than the glitch immunity are ignored and pulses shorter than tDEBOUNCE do not reach /PBOUT. A valid press gives a low pulse on /PBOUT of at least tINT_Min; a press held longer than tDEBOUNCE + tINT_Min keeps /PBOUT low until release.

Open-drain outputs (/RST, /INT, /PBOUT, /VCCLO) each need a pull-up; 10 kΩ is enough in most designs. The push-pull enable output needs none. A capacitor on VREF is required even if the reference is not used, 1 µF recommended. VCC takes a 0.1 µF decoupling capacitor close to the pin. The CSRD capacitor sets tSRD and should be low-ESR, such as ceramic.
Reflow peak 260 °C, with no more than 30 s above 255 °C.
